study: studies/identifiability/lag-forgetting (lag_forgetting.py) -- is lag_bands' decay forgetting of A or the edge weakening?
note: Literature-review analysis 1 for Paper II F1 (Cepeda et al. 2008; Matayoshi et al. 2025). Pre-registered before any real read (62fb970). FLOOR FAILED TWICE, so every registered verdict is UNANSWERABLE and the programme verdict is UNRESOLVED. v1 (one recent A reading held at R=1) read pure forgetting as EDGE-WEAKENS 3/3 (guess contamination); the CHANGES entry (49206aa, before real data) moved to a Wald split (arm fixed before the reading; drop = E x A-gap). v2 never confused worlds but missed on power (EDGE 2/3, HUMP shape 2/3); the same floor at 9,000 learners passes (diagnostic, gates nothing). POSITIVITY: XES3G5M UNANSWERABLE (17 held pairs; 0.7% of >=7-day cases re-attempt A within a day of B). As computed, not findings: Eedi share explained +1.05 [+0.81, +1.43], E flat 0.686 -> 0.694, the A gap closing because non-masters' current A accuracy rises (0.381 -> 0.445) while masters' does not fall; ASSISTments and EdNet show no decay on the re-attempt subset (NO-DECAY-TO-SPLIT). DESCRIPTIVE (lag_bands' arms and pairs): the gap closes because the disadvantaged arm rises in ASSISTments, XES3G5M and Eedi, the floor's edge-world signature, not its forgetting one. No rise-then-fall anywhere (largest drop in the first hour in all four corpora), but the shape verdict is UNANSWERABLE. F1 keeps both readings. Moves nothing.
